Detections of each occasion over the draws of the calibration

Source: R/occasion_draws.R
occasion_draws.Rd

Turns an export of export_occupancy_data() with calibration draws into one version of the detection data per posterior draw: in each draw, an occasion is a detection when at least one of its predictions is judged true. Any occupancy software can then fit its model to each version and pool the posteriors, so that the uncertainty of the calibration reaches the ecological estimates (Monte Carlo propagation). This is the occasion-level counterpart of history_draws(), which works by night.

Usage

occasion_draws(
  export_dir,
  species = NULL,
  rule = c("sample", "threshold"),
  p_min = 0.95,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = 2026,
  write = TRUE
)

Arguments

export_dir

Folder written by export_occupancy_data() with fit.

species

Optional species to process, matched against species (the short code, e.g. "phy_cuv") or species_code of detections.csv. All species with calibration draws by default.

rule

"sample" or "threshold"; see Rules.

p_min

Threshold of rule = "threshold".

n_draws

Optional number of calibration draws to use: the first ones, in increasing order of their identifiers. All by default.

seed

Seed of rule = "sample".

write

Write occasion_draws.parquet in export_dir and record it in schema.json (schema version 1.2)? An existing table is replaced.

Value

A tibble with draw, site, occasion_id, species and y (1 detection, 0 none, NA not scored), with one row per draw and occasion with at least one exported prediction of the species. The other occasions of occasions.csv are non-detections in every draw. Returned invisibly when write = TRUE.

Rules

With rule = "sample" (default), a prediction whose probability of being true is p in a draw is judged true with probability p, so no threshold is involved; this assumes that the predictions of an occasion are true or false independently, given the calibration. With rule = "threshold", it is judged true when p >= p_min, as in history_draws(); this keeps only the predictions the calibration is nearly sure of and gives fewer detections.

Matching

A prediction takes the value of the grid point nearest its score and of the calibration keys of its occasion (schema.json$calibration$keys, e.g. the month). An occasion with a prediction that has no calibration draws (a species, site or key level absent from calibration_draws.parquet) cannot be scored: it is NA in every draw, with a warning, not a non-detection.

Reproducibility

The random numbers follow those of crywolf::fp_draws_data(), so that both give the same detections for the same export, rule and seed: the seed is set once per species with R's default generators (Mersenne-Twister, Inversion, Rejection), and each draw, in increasing order of its identifier, takes one uniform number per scored prediction, in the order of detections.csv. The first n draws of a call are therefore the same as those of a call with n_draws = n. Species are processed one at a time, in alphabetical order, each from the seed. The global random number generator is left as it was.

See also

export_occupancy_data(), history_draws(), vignette("crywolf-integration").
